failures.title: Alfa Romeo 955B1000 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: MultiAir Unit Failure - misfiring and loss of power
items.whatHappens: The MultiAir system uses electro‑hydraulic valves to control intake valve lift and timing. The unit can fail due to clogged oil filters (the MultiAir filter is separate from the main oil filter), low oil pressure, or solenoid issues. Symptoms include misfiring, rough idle, loss of power, and the engine running on three cylinders. The issue is often temperature‑related.
items.repairVsReplace: MultiAir unit replacement is a standalone repair but is expensive - typically £800-£1,500. Regular oil changes with the correct MultiAir‑spec oil and MultiAir filter changes are essential for prevention.

items.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - direct injection drawback
items.whatHappens: Like all direct‑injection petrol engines, the 955B1000's intake valves can accumulate carbon deposits over time. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, reduced fuel economy, and eventual misfires.
items.repairVsReplace: Carbon cleaning (walnut blasting) is a standalone service costing £300-£600. Preventative use of top‑tier fuels and occasional Italian tune‑ups are recommended.

items.title: Turbocharger Issues - wastegate and actuator wear
items.whatHappens: The small Garrett turbocharger can suffer from wastegate actuator wear or sticking, leading to boost control issues. Symptoms include loss of power, hesitation, and check engine lights for underboost/overboost conditions.
items.repairVsReplace: Actuator replacement is a standalone repair (£200-£400). If the turbo itself is worn (play in the shaft), a full turbo replacement is required (£600-£1,200).

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 955B1000
variants.intro: The 955B1000 is the Euro 6, 140 hp version of Alfa Romeo's 1.4‑litre MultiAir turbo engine, produced from 2015 to 2018. It features MultiAir electro‑hydraulic valve actuation, a Garrett turbocharger, and multi‑point fuel injection. It is the most powerful petrol option offered in the MiTo facelift. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped plate on the front of the engine - On the V5C registration document - under engine number - Via an Alfa Romeo VIN decoder - the engine code is part of the vehicle identification Commonly confused codes: - 955A1000 - the earlier Euro 5 1.4 MultiAir 140hp engine (2010-2015), with different emissions calibration and ECU; not a direct swap without ECU changes - 955A3000 - the 1.75‑litre TBi engine used in the Giulietta QV and MiTo Cloverleaf; completely different displacement and architecture - 198A4.000 - the 1.4 MultiAir used in Fiat models (Punto, 500); similar architecture but different ECU calibration and emissions

relatives.description: the earlier Euro 5 version of the 1.4 MultiAir engine (2010-2015), producing the same 140 hp but with different emissions calibration and ECU mapping. The 955B1000 is essentially the Euro 6 version, introduced to meet stricter emissions standards. The physical engine is very similar, but the ECUs are not interchangeable. [955A3000 Engine - /alfa-romeo/955a3000-engine/]

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 955B1000 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 955B1000 is a viable option for MiTo owners, with units available from breakers at £1,200-£1,700. However, the MultiAir unit is the critical component - only buy with documented service history showing regular MultiAir oil filter changes and correct 5W‑40 oil. A used unit without history is a gamble; budget for MultiAir servicing. Used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper 955B1000 recon addresses the engine's known weaknesses: new MultiAir unit (or thorough rebuild of the existing unit), new timing belt, water pump, full gasket set, and carbon cleaning of the intake valves. This is the right call for owners who want a reliable, long‑lasting unit - the MultiAir engine is a delight when properly refreshed. Expect £1,700-£2,100 with 12-24 months warranty. Reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full 955B1000 rebuild is rarely justified given the relatively low cost of reconditioned units. It is only sensible for owners of rare MiTo variants (e.g., Racer, special editions) or those who want to upgrade with forged internals. Costs exceed £2,200-£2,800. Rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** Our vetted UK Alfa Romeo specialists offer supply‑only or full supply‑and‑fit - 12‑month warranty on reconditioned units, nationwide delivery. Supply and fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 955B1000 sits in Alfa Romeo MiTos now worth £2,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage. A reconditioned engine at £1,700-£2,100 represents 20‑60% of vehicle value - a significant investment. For a high‑mileage MiTo worth under £3,000, a used unit with documented MultiAir service history may be the most sensible option. Evaluate the car's overall condition - these are modern classics, and condition is everything.

MultiAir unit failure requires expensive replacement (£800-£1,500). Carbon buildup requires walnut blasting (£300-£600). items.question: Which Alfa Romeo models have the 955B1000 engine?
items.answer: The 955B1000 is fitted exclusively to the Alfa Romeo MiTo facelift (2015-2018) in the 140 hp MultiAir turbo petrol variant. It is the Euro 6 version of the 1.4‑litre MultiAir engine. The earlier 955A1000 is the Euro 5 version (2010-2015).

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 955B1000?
items.answer: A reconditioned 955B1000 is the safer choice because it addresses the engine's known weak points (MultiAir unit, carbon deposits, timing belt) and comes with a warranty. Used units are cheaper but risk MultiAir unit failure. Given the age of all 955B1000s (2015-2018), reconditioning is recommended for reliability.

items.question: How do I know if my MiTo has the 955B1000 or the earlier 955A1000?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the block (front of the engine) and listed on your V5C or via an Alfa Romeo VIN decoder. The 955B1000 is the Euro 6 140 hp MultiAir (2015-2018). The 955A1000 is the Euro 5 140 hp MultiAir (2010-2015). The two engines are not interchangeable without significant ECU work.

items.question: Is the 955B1000 a reliable engine?
items.answer: The 955B1000 is a characterful engine that rewards regular maintenance - reliability depends entirely on service history. MultiAir units fail if oil and filter changes are neglected. Direct injection causes carbon buildup that requires occasional cleaning. A well‑maintained 955B1000 can exceed 100,000 miles.
